# Part V: Forensic Tests for Audit {.unnumbered}

This part brings together the tests that auditors run again and again on transaction data. Checking records against the rules; Benford's law and Nigrini's tests for manipulated amounts; finding duplicates, exact and fuzzy; linking records of the same person across lists; finding gaps in sequences; and reconstructing a process from a system's audit trail to see whether its steps were followed.

Each test produces a list of exceptions. Remember that an exception is a lead, to be verified against the records, and not yet a finding.

The chapters in this part are:

- @sec-validate, checking data against a rule book.
- @sec-benford, Benford's law for first and second digits.
- @sec-nigrini, largest subsets, round numbers, amounts just below limits and other tests.
- @sec-dup, exact, near and fuzzy duplicates.
- @sec-linkage, finding the same person in two lists.
- @sec-gaps, missing numbers and dates in sequences.
- @sec-process, checking whether a process was followed, from a system's audit trail.
